title: Protect an invariant under concurrent transactions
description: Choose a business operation, isolation level, and application guard. Increase overlap to see whether PostgreSQL prevents the anomaly, rejects work for retry, or makes writers wait.

isolationLevels.label: Read Committed
isolationLevels.detail: Each statement gets a fresh snapshot. This is PostgreSQL's default and allows multi-statement read drift.

isolationLevels.label: Repeatable Read
isolationLevels.detail: One transaction snapshot prevents read drift, but snapshot isolation can still permit write skew.

isolationLevels.label: Serializable
isolationLevels.detail: SSI rejects dangerous dependency structures so committed transactions behave like a serial order.

guards.label: No explicit guard
guards.detail: Read state, decide in application code, then write without locking the decision boundary.

guards.label: Lock the decision row
guards.detail: Use SELECT FOR UPDATE on the row that owns the invariant and acquire locks in a stable order.

guards.label: Atomic predicate or constraint
guards.detail: Move the check into one conditional statement or a database-enforced uniqueness or exclusion rule.

guards.label: Bounded transaction retry
guards.detail: Retry the complete unit of work after serialization failure with a fresh snapshot and bounded backoff.

scenarios.label: Reserve the final seats
scenarios.detail: Several writers observe remaining capacity, then create reservations for different customers.
scenarios.invariant: Confirmed reservation quantity must never exceed venue capacity.

none.explanation: Independent snapshots can each validate an old aggregate before any writer changes the shared decision state.

decision-lock.explanation: Locking one capacity owner serializes the check and reservation update around the invariant.

atomic-predicate.explanation: A conditional capacity update moves the check and state change into one database decision.

retry-loop.explanation: Retries recover rejected serializable transactions, but retries alone do not prevent write skew at weaker isolation.

scenarios.label: Apply a balance debit
scenarios.detail: Workers read one account balance, calculate a replacement value, and update the same row.
scenarios.invariant: Accepted debits must not disappear and the account must not cross its permitted limit.
scenarios.failureMode: A stale read can overwrite another debit

none.explanation: A read-modify-write sequence at Read Committed can calculate from stale state and replace a newer value.

decision-lock.explanation: A row lock makes each debit observe the balance left by the previous committed writer.

atomic-predicate.explanation: UPDATE with a balance predicate lets PostgreSQL lock, recheck, and change the row atomically.

retry-loop.explanation: A retry loop handles database conflicts but cannot detect a logical overwrite that committed successfully.

scenarios.label: Build a consistent report
scenarios.detail: A transaction reads several related aggregates while application writes continue.
scenarios.invariant: Every value in the report must describe the same committed point in time.
scenarios.failureMode: Statement snapshots can produce a mixed-time report

none.explanation: Read Committed may use a different snapshot for each statement, so related totals can describe different moments.

decision-lock.explanation: Locking all contributing rows is expensive and fragile; a stable transaction snapshot is the cleaner read-only boundary.

atomic-predicate.explanation: An atomic write predicate does not give several report queries one shared snapshot.

retry-loop.explanation: Repeating a Read Committed report can still mix statement snapshots; choose a stable snapshot instead.
